answer: Two keys must not share one flood-control seat. Each applicant is assigned one numbered notch on a published basalt weir at km 14.6 of the live delta, and only that key may seat a serialized jade staff-gauge during a 17-minute slack window. Clerks publish H=blake3(addr||notch_id||staff_serial||gauge_mm||window_id). Filing costs 0.31 POA; a 23 POA bond locks nine epochs. Auditors photograph the seated staff against the weir stamp and re-read the gauge on the tide sheet. A reused notch, borrowed staff, or failed jade socket assay seizes the bond and benches both keys for fourteen epochs.
